criteria.blocker: TWO CLAUSES FAIL, both named in the criterion. (1) RESPONSIVE ACCESSIBILITY — the only axe assertion anywhere on Home is features/__tests__/modules-content-a11y.test.tsx:233-250, 'Module-level a11y — Home/Dashboard (HomeSectionBoundary)', which renders the 40-line HomeSectionBoundary and nothing else. My own enumeration (`grep -rl 'axe|toHaveNoViolations' --include='*.test.tsx' --include='*.test.ts' .` under frontend/, node_modules excluded) returns 23 files; NONE covers home-widget-grid.tsx, any of the 11 widgets, the stat-card row, dashboard-deferred-body.tsx, or any of the four /me/* self-service pages (features/employee-self-service has zero test files of any kind). No viewport/rendered measurement was taken by any pass — 'responsive' is a source reading, not a measurement. (2) REPRESENTATIVE E2E — src/modules/dashboard/dashboard.controller.e2e-spec.ts is 53 lines and contains exactly one test, `it.each(routes)("401 on %s %s without a token")` over an 18-tuple route table; `grep -c 'it('` returns 0 because it is a single it.each. There is no authenticated path, no per-permission allow/deny, no cross-tenant case, and no degraded-section case. It has NOT been run by any pass: it needs `pnpm test:e2e`, and `grep -c AUTH_SIGNING_KEYS .env` in the backend returns 0 (the key is absent), which test/helpers/sign-token.ts:44 throws on. `find src test -name '*seeded-e2e-spec.ts'` returns 11 files (billing, crm x3, db, kb, perf, security x3, support) — none for dashboard, home or self-service. Separately, check:module-lifecycle exits 2 and contributes NO module-gating verdict in either direction: /tmp/beg-check_module-lifecycle.log reads 'PREREQUISITE UNMET — cannot determine — APP_DATABASE_URL is not set', and it covers one module (timesheets, 11 tables) regardless. To close: add axe + viewport coverage for the widget grid, the widgets and the four /me/* pages, and write an authenticated/allow-deny/cross-tenant Home e2e that is actually run (which needs AUTH_SIGNING_KEYS in .env or a documented dev key).

criteria.evidence: I ran the proof myself: `pnpm exec jest --maxWorkers=2 --testPathPattern="dashboard-home-fanout"` in streamlineos-backend — EXIT=0, 1 suite / 14 tests, 15.754 s (/tmp/v-fanout.log). Every clause of the criterion has a measured test that bites. CONCURRENT: 'PRD-C144 — Home sections fan out CONCURRENTLY' routes the personal-dashboard sources through a barrier that only opens once N distinct sections have reported in, so a sequential implementation deadlocks; the companion 'BITE: the barrier really does deadlock a sequential fanout' proves the barrier is not permissive. BOUNDED: 'MEASURED: fanout width does not grow with the tenant's enabled-module count' and 'MEASURED: module-availability probes are capped by the static registry, not by the tenant' — src/modules/dashboard/dashboard-scope.ts:36-46 derives the probe set from `DASHBOARD_HOME_SECTIONS.filter(isModuleSection)` deduped through a Set, i.e. a compile-time constant, never from the tenant's enabled modules. Every list read inside the sections is capped: dashboard-read-limits.ts declares DASHBOARD_LIST_CAP=100, DASHBOARD_ATTENDANCE_ROW_CAP=500, DASHBOARD_PROJECT_ID_CAP=200. RENDERS AVAILABLE SECTIONS WITHOUT WAITING FOR THE SLOWEST: dashboard-section-settle.ts:16 HOME_SECTION_DEADLINE_MS=2_500 and :58 `timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(DEADLINE), deadlineMs)`, with 'MEASURED: getPersonalDashboard answers with two sections while the third hangs forever' (2505 ms), 'MEASURED: a hanging organization lookup still yields the employee and project counts' (2510 ms), 'MEASURED: settleSection abandons a source that never settles and degrades only it', 'MEASURED: a fast source is never charged the deadline' and 'MEASURED: a rejection after the deadline never becomes an unhandled rejection'. The prologue that gates the fanout is covered too — 'PRD-C144 — the fanout PROLOGUE is deadline-protected and fails closed' has three hang tests (module gate, membership lookup, permission gate, each ~2.5 s) plus 'BITE: the same harness with a resolving gate produces the counts, so the assertions above are not vacuous'. FRONTEND HALF: features/dashboard/home-section-independence.test.tsx asserts on rendered output (one section answered, one loading, one rejected) and home-section-boundary.test.tsx enforces a per-widget boundary by source scan for all named widgets; both pass in the 65-test frontend run above. This CLOSES 06-audit.md's F2, which claimed at its head that the deadline did not cover the prologue — at this head it does, in both aggregates.
